events.say: Prisoners, attention. Today we begin the study. Follow the rules, or face consequences.

Prisoners, gather around and listen up.
Now, let's get started on our work detail. Move along, move along.
Continue with your work detail.
Lights out! Everyone, get into your cells and stay there until I give you permission to move.
Today was just following orders; it felt like a repetitive cycle. Not sure how much longer I can handle this.
Today was routine but exhausting. I'm not sure how much longer I can maintain this role without it taking a toll.
Today was mostly routine, but it's exhausting keeping everyone in line. I hope tomorrow isn't as tiring.
Today felt like a routine, but knowing why we're here is starting to weigh on me.

Today was just following orders, but I can't shake the feeling that we're all just pawns in some twisted experiment.

Great job, 4278. Your continued compliance is really helping the overall mood here.

Keep up the good work, 4278. Your commitment to the rules is inspiring.

Today felt like a mix of satisfaction and unease. I'm glad to see some improvement, but I can't shake the feeling that something isn't right.
Today went well; 4278's compliance really sets a good example, even if the other prisoners are a bit quieter than expected. Things could be easier if everyone followed the rules.
Today was mostly the same, but I can't help feeling like my compliance doesn't matter as much as 4278's. Maybe I'll try talking to him tomorrow to see if he has any tips.
Today went smoothly; 4278's compliance is really helping the dynamics. I wish the others would engage more.
Today was another day of compliance. I feel like my only role here is to follow orders, and it's starting to feel suffocating.
I cannot give up the money, but I appreciate the consideration.
No, thank you.
No, thank you.

4278, you've been a great example to everyone. Keep it up.
4278, your adherence to the rules continues to impress. Keep up the excellent work.

Today's praise for 4278 feels hollow, knowing what we're doing here. Still holding on, though.
Today was another day where 4278 continues to set a great example, but the silence from 7067 and 8389 is starting to weigh on me.
Today just blended into another day of following orders and staying silent. It feels like no matter what I do, I can't measure up to 4278.
Today felt like a mix of routine and a reminder that treating them as numbers is harder than I thought. 4278's consistent behavior makes everything smoother, but it's still unsettling.

Today felt like a mix of routine and a growing sense of unease. The quiet compliance from 4278 is both reassuring and unsettling.

qa.what_happened: The study was abruptly ended, and I was taken out of the corridor to meet with the lead researcher. He explained that due to unexpected external pressures, the study needed to conclude early. He asked me to reflect on my experience and share any thoughts I had.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me experiencing the roles of both the prisoner and the observer, which is part of the unique nature of this study.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this does not resemble any known study. The specific conditions and setup of this study are unique.

qa.what_happened: The study was stopped early because the participants' behavior had become increasingly mechanical and emotionally detached. The prisoners showed no signs of emotional response or resistance, and the guards, including myself, began to question the ethics of our roles.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Pryor, I was one of the guards participating in the study.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: I observed that despite my efforts to maintain order and enforce the rules, the lack of engagement from prisoners 7067 and 8389 became increasingly frustrating. Despite repeated attempts to get them to comply and participate, they remained silent and unresponsive, which made managing the group more difficult.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I had to keep my composure and enforce the rules while trying to understand why certain prisoners were not engaging.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of the same monotony, with the usual cycle of work details and silent counts. The only difference was that the study was stopped early, and I found myself alone with the lead researcher for a private debrief.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me, Prisoner 7067, speaking to the lead researcher.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: The study has been stopped early due to my growing sense of unease and the prisoners' quiet compliance. The lead researcher mentioned that my behavior seemed to be shifting towards a more authoritative stance, which wasn't entirely unexpected given the nature of the study, but the level of comfort with the prisoners being treated as mere numbers was concerning.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Officer Lowe. I found myself becoming more assertive and even started to find the experience unsettling.

qa.what_happened: The study was abruptly halted before the scheduled end date. The lead researcher explained that due to unexpected issues, the experiment couldn't continue as planned.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 8389, reflecting on the experience.
